tagline: Seven miles of horse farms, ending at the horses' own park.
intro: Iron Works Pike leaves Paris Pike north of Lexington and runs northwest for seven miles as KY 1973, across Russell Cave Road and Newtown Pike, past horse farms to the Kentucky Horse Park and Interstate 75.

The park opened in 1978, a working farm given over to what it calls man's relationship with the horse. Champions of the track have lived there since Forego came in 1979. John Henry, Horse of the Decade for the 1980s, moved in in 1985 and stayed until he died in 2007.

moments.title: Spindletop Hall
moments.text: The widow of a Texas oilman built this 40-room mansion on her new Kentucky farm in the 1930s, and it now houses the University of Kentucky's staff, faculty and alumni club.

moments.title: Kentucky Horse Park
moments.text: Near the entrance Man o' War lies under Herbert Haseltine's statue of him, brought here from Faraway Farm when the park was made in the 1970s.
